import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Dog Registration Analysis in Zurich, Switzerland', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Plot 1: Top 10 Dog Breeds
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
top_breeds = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().head(10)
colors1 = sns.color_palette('viridis', 10)
bars1 = ax1.barh(range(len(top_breeds)), top_breeds.values, color=colors1)
ax1.set_yticks(range(len(top_breeds)))
ax1.set_yticklabels(top_breeds.index)
ax1.invert_yaxis()
ax1.set_xlabel('Number of Registrations')
ax1.set_title('Top 10 Most Popular Dog Breeds', fontweight='bold')
for i, v in enumerate(top_breeds.values):
    ax1.text(v + 100, i, str(v), va='center', fontsize=9)

# Plot 2: Dog Registrations by District (Kreis)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
district_counts = df.groupby('KreisLang')['AnzHunde'].sum().sort_values(ascending=True)
colors2 = sns.color_palette('coolwarm', len(district_counts))
bars2 = ax2.barh(range(len(district_counts)), district_counts.values, color=colors2)
ax2.set_yticks(range(len(district_counts)))
ax2.set_yticklabels(district_counts.index)
ax2.set_xlabel('Total Number of Dogs')
ax2.set_title('Dog Registrations by District', fontweight='bold')

# Plot 3: Dog Age Distribution
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
# Clean and sort age data
age_order = df[['AlterVHundLang', 'AlterVHundSort']].drop_duplicates().sort_values('AlterVHundSort')
age_counts = df['AlterVHundLang'].value_counts().reindex(age_order['AlterVHundLang'].values)
age_counts = age_counts.dropna()
colors3 = sns.color_palette('Blues_d', len(age_counts))
ax3.bar(range(len(age_counts)), age_counts.values, color=colors3)
ax3.set_xticks(range(len(age_counts)))
ax3.set_xticklabels(age_counts.index, rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=8)
ax3.set_xlabel('Dog Age Category')
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Dogs')
ax3.set_title('Distribution of Dog Ages', fontweight='bold')

# Plot 4: Owner Age vs Dog Gender Distribution
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
# Create a cross-tabulation of owner age and dog gender
owner_dog_gender = pd.crosstab(df['AlterV10Lang'], df['SexHundLang'])
# Sort by owner age
owner_age_order = df[['AlterV10Lang', 'AlterV10Sort']].drop_duplicates().sort_values('AlterV10Sort')
owner_dog_gender = owner_dog_gender.reindex(owner_age_order['AlterV10Lang'].values).dropna()

x = range(len(owner_dog_gender))
width = 0.35
if 'männlich' in owner_dog_gender.columns and 'weiblich' in owner_dog_gender.columns:
    bars_male = ax4.bar([i - width/2 for i in x], owner_dog_gender['männlich'], width, label='Male Dogs', color='steelblue')
    bars_female = ax4.bar([i + width/2 for i in x], owner_dog_gender['weiblich'], width, label='Female Dogs', color='coral')
else:
    # Fallback if column names are different
    cols = owner_dog_gender.columns[:2]
    bars1 = ax4.bar([i - width/2 for i in x], owner_dog_gender[cols[0]], width, label=cols[0], color='steelblue')
    bars2 = ax4.bar([i + width/2 for i in x], owner_dog_gender[cols[1]], width, label=cols[1], color='coral')

ax4.set_xticks(x)
ax4.set_xticklabels(owner_dog_gender.index, rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=8)
ax4.set_xlabel('Owner Age Group')
ax4.set_ylabel('Number of Dogs')
ax4.set_title('Dog Gender by Owner Age Group', fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend()

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
